_comment: Example workspace configuration. Copy to $COFFERDAM_HOME/config/workspaces.json
and edit on the workstation — this file is an example and is never read by the
service.
A workspace is a stable name for WHAT YOU ARE WORKING ON, bound to a project that
already exists in task-projects.json. It carries the objective, the expected next
step and a few continuity references; the project carries the directory and the
adapters.
A workspace never says WHERE: there is no 'root' and no 'path'. The directory
belongs to the project it names, which is where root validation, the symlink walk
and the re-check before every task already live.
A workspace never says WHO RUNS: there is no 'adapters', 'delegated_adapter',
'model' or 'provider'. Which agent runs is the project's decision (PR #34), and a
workspace that could name one would put that authority back where ordering used
to be. An entry carrying one of those fields is refused by name.
'project_id' must name a project in task-projects.json. It is checked for shape at
load and for existence at use, so a workspace written before its project is added
stays in the file and reports the missing project rather than disappearing.
Nothing is auto-registered. Cofferdam never creates a workspace for a project it
finds, and there is no API route that writes this file.
Document roles (plan_doc, status_doc, decisions_doc) and evaluation profiles are
NOT in this schema yet. They arrive with the components that read them — the mind
in M2J PR2/PR3, evaluation depth in M2K. A field nothing reads is a field somebody
builds on before it means anything.
See docs/WORKSPACES.md.

workspaces.notes: disabled: configured but not something to activate by accident
